metadata.title: Cross-Disciplinary Technology Tree of Modern Science (DAG)
metadata.description: A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) cross-disciplinary network of modern scientific sub-disciplines originating from four empirical precursors: Astronomy, Surveying, Alchemy, and Anatomy (adapted for D3.js / 3d-force-graph / Three.js rendering)

nodes.name: Astronomical Observation & Navigational Calendrics
nodes.description: Shattered the Aristotelian cosmos and formulated mathematical laws of celestial motion through precise naked-eye astronomical observations and navigational calendar reforms.

nodes.name: Geodetic Surveying & Ballistic Craftsmanship
nodes.description: Introduced 'quantitative measurement' and 'error control' into natural inquiry through military ballistic computation, cartographic surveying, and mechanical horology.

nodes.name: Alchemy, Metallurgy & Iatrochemical Distillation
nodes.description: Accumulated extensive experimental techniques and reaction vessels for substance separation, purification, and calcination, building the experimental repertoire for modern chemistry.

nodes.name: Human Anatomy & Natural History
nodes.description: Rejected Galenic dogma and established an empirical tradition of biological structure through hands-on dissection and morphological observation.

nodes.name: Analytic Geometry & Calculus
nodes.description: Translated spatial geometric measurement into algebraic equations and provided a universal mathematical language for describing continuous motion and instantaneous rates of change.

nodes.name: Geometric Optics & Telescope/Microscope
nodes.description: Combined lens-grinding craftsmanship with geometry, extending human vision bidirectionally toward the macrocosm (celestial bodies) and the microcosm (cells).

nodes.name: Classical Mechanics & Universal Gravitation
nodes.description: Unified terrestrial ballistic measurements and celestial planetary orbits under an axiomatic system of calculus and mechanics, establishing the paradigm of modern physics.

nodes.name: Pneumatic Experiments & Boyle's Law
nodes.description: Transformed alchemy by introducing precision barometric measurement and air pumps, proposing the scientific concept of a 'chemical element'.

nodes.name: Blood Circulation & Experimental Physiology
key_elements: Hydraulic Pump Model of the Heart
nodes.description: Introduced mechanical measurement (hydraulic pump capacity calculation) into vascular anatomy, proving blood circulation and inaugurating quantitative experimental physiology.

nodes.name: Microscopic Anatomy & Discovery of the Cell
nodes.description: Surpassed the limits of naked-eye dissection with optical microscopes, discovering cellular structures and the microbial world.

nodes.name: Analytical Mechanics & Fluid Mechanics
nodes.description: Fully analyticalized and variationalized classical mechanics, laying the mathematical framework for continuum media (fluids, elastic solids) and future quantum mechanics.

nodes.name: Thermodynamics & Statistical Physics
nodes.description: Originated from steam-engine efficiency measurements and gas studies, bridging macroscopic thermal work with microscopic random molecular motion.

nodes.name: Electromagnetism & Maxwell's Equations
nodes.description: Starting from bioelectricity and electrochemistry, ultimately unified electricity, magnetism, and light into Maxwell's partial differential equations.

nodes.name: Modern Quantitative Chemistry & Atomic Theory
nodes.description: Ended the phlogiston theory through rigorous precision weighing, establishing quantitative conservation laws in chemical reactions and the atomic-molecular theory.

nodes.name: Organic Synthesis & Periodic Law of Elements
nodes.description: Broke the 'vitalism' barrier between inorganic and organic matter and systematically revealed the periodic intrinsic laws of chemical elements.

nodes.name: Modern Geology & Paleontology
nodes.description: Combined geodetic surveying with comparative anatomy of fossils to reconstruct the deep-time evolutionary history of the Earth.

nodes.name: Cell Theory, Microbiology & Theory of Evolution
nodes.description: Consolidated biology into a unified modern science across two dimensions: microscopic cellular unity and macroscopic evolutionary history.

nodes.name: Probability, Statistics, Group Theory & Non-Euclidean Geometry
nodes.description: Arising from astronomical surveying error processing and higher algebra, providing core mathematical tools for relativity, quantum physics, and modern experimental statistics.

nodes.name: Special & General Relativity
key_elements: Invariance of the Speed of Light
nodes.description: Reconciled the conflict between classical mechanics and Maxwellian electromagnetism, reconstructing the nature of spacetime and gravity via Riemannian geometry.

nodes.name: Quantum Mechanics & Nuclear Physics
nodes.description: Revealed the quantized laws governing microscopic particles, completely bridging the fundamental boundary between physics and atomic/chemical structures.

nodes.name: Solid-State Physics & Semiconductor Theory
nodes.description: Applied quantum mechanics and group theory to analyze periodic crystal structures, directly giving birth to the transistor and the modern microelectronics industry.

nodes.name: Physical Chemistry & Quantum Chemistry
key_elements: Hybrid Orbitals & Nature of the Chemical Bond
nodes.description: Comprehensively reshaped chemistry with thermodynamics and quantum mechanics, explaining molecular configurations and chemical reaction rates from first principles.

nodes.name: Polymer Chemistry & Modern Materials Science
nodes.description: Combined organic synthesis with solid-state microscopic characterization to enable on-demand design of macromolecules and specialized engineering materials.

nodes.name: Mendelian Genetics & Biochemistry
nodes.description: Introduced probability and statistics into biological hybridization and used organic chemistry to decipher intracellular metabolic enzymatic reaction networks.

nodes.name: Molecular Biology & The Central Dogma
nodes.description: The pinnacle convergence of physics (X-ray diffraction, quantum chemical bonds), genetics, and biochemistry, unlocking the molecular code of biological heredity.

nodes.name: Electronic Engineering, Cybernetics & Information Theory
nodes.description: Integrated mathematical logic, probability statistics, and electronic circuits to establish the universal paradigm of 'information, computation, and feedback control'.

nodes.name: Modern Astrophysics & Cosmology
nodes.description: Deeply merged macrocosmic relativity with microcosmic nuclear and particle physics to address the origin of the universe, stellar evolution, and dark matter/dark energy.

nodes.name: Computer Science & Artificial Intelligence
key_elements: Deep Neural Networks & Large Language Models
nodes.description: Combined semiconductor hardware with information algorithms to become the fourth-paradigm foundation empowering all scientific disciplines after mathematics and measurement.

nodes.name: Genomics, Bioinformatics & Synthetic Biology
nodes.description: Fused molecular biology with computer algorithms and engineering, propelling humanity from 'reading the code of life' to 'writing and designing life'.

nodes.name: Cognitive Neuroscience & Brain Science
nodes.description: The ultimate convergence of anatomy, electrophysiological physics, molecular biology, and artificial intelligence in exploring human consciousness and brain mechanisms.

nodes.name: Earth System Science & Climate Dynamics
nodes.description: Integrates geology, fluid mechanics, geochemistry, and supercomputing to study the Earth's atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere as a coupled complex system.

nodes.name: Nanotechnology & Quantum Information Science
nodes.description: Manipulates matter and information at the single-atom and quantum-state scale, breaking classical Moore's Law and macroscopic material limits.
